neighbours.label: the build-up to a rest or break after effort ('give your brain a', 'much deserved', 'take frequent')
fire: After a long shift, give your legs a rest for an hour.
He was enjoying a well deserved break at the beach.
In hot weather, work slowly and take regular breaks.
After that exam, give your mind a rest this weekend.
She finally took a much needed holiday by the lake.
Stop every hour on the drive and take short breaks.
Study for a while, then rest your eyes.
We all earned a nice long break after the harvest.
quiet: After a long shift, give your boss a report for the file.
He was reading a very old novel at the beach.
In hot weather, sell cold drinks and take card payments.
After that exam, give your teacher a call this weekend.
She finally bought a much bigger house by the lake.
Stop every hour on the drive and check the map.
Study for a while, then read your notes.
We all sold a nice long fence after the harvest.

short: build-up to a rest or break
notes: Near misses in probes were not clean: 'take plenty of water' 0.46, 'take a bus ... Christmas' 0.37. So 'take' and holidays may do part of this.
